title: PROP-113 full design + PROP-051-grade smoke-test plan — author concrete workspace-sync.md edits (Fix A two-sided gate, Fix B robust set-build, Fix C post-sync assertion), per-phase smoke-test procedure, disaster-vector analysis, and rollback plan. Propose-only; operator reviews + selects phase to ship.
context:
PROP-113 was authored 2026-06-22T02:40Z (tinker FND-01) and proposes 3 layered fixes for the prune↔workspace-sync re-add loop that's still resurrecting ~150 integrity artifacts/day despite PROP-094 + PROP-099 + PROP-103. PROP-113's status is 'pending' / propose_only:true / requires_human_judgment. The operator considered shipping immediately but the target file (monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md) is PROP-051 disaster-sensitive — that file produced the 2026-05-21 mass-delete (14.9M lines wiped from origin/main) and any edit needs disaster-grade smoke-test per PROP-110 Q7.

What PROP-113 already states:
  - Fix A: two-sided trust gate — also set GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED=1 when `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES` (or 1.5× ARCHIVE_LINES). Closes the 70,375-vs-20,631 overcount that escaped PROP-103's lower-bound-only gate.
  - Fix B: robust set build — stream-parse archive JSONL with malformed-fragment tolerance, validate each emitted path against regex `^monitor/integrity/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$` before sort -u. Addresses root cause (multi-line `body:` fields in verify-pending-runs-archive.jsonl corrupting the line-split).
  - Fix C: post-sync resurrection assertion — call `node monitor/scripts/check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 2` at end of each workspace-sync run; on RC=3 write `workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json` + loud agent_note instead of silent success.

What's MISSING from PROP-113 (this directive asks tinker to author):
  - Concrete bash diffs to workspace-sync.md for each fix (not just philosophy). The operator wants to be able to apply each fix as a discrete edit with copy-pastable old_string/new_string blocks for /tmp/edit-clone work.
  - PROP-051-grade smoke-test plan per phase (A only, A+C, A+B+C). 'Disaster-grade' here means: (i) verify the edit doesn't introduce a new mass-delete vector; (ii) verify the existing fail-closed SKIP path still fires correctly when the trust gate trips; (iii) verify a known-good cycle still ships (cp the just-tombstoned paths is SKIPPED, all other workspace-only files commit normally); (iv) recovery procedure if shipping the fix triggers an unexpected abort.
  - Disaster-vector analysis: what's the worst case if each fix has a bug? E.g., Fix A's stricter gate could fire MORE often than intended, hard-skipping prune-managed categories indefinitely; Fix B's stream-parser could mis-classify legitimate archive lines as malformed; Fix C's resurrection assertion could falsely abort if check-prune-resurrection.js has its own bug. For each: how would we DETECT the bug, and how would we ROLL BACK?
  - Sequence recommendation: ship A only first, observe, then B+C? Or all 3 together? PROP-113's executive_summary suggests all 3 but the operator wants the trade-off framed explicitly.
  - Backfill cleanup: 312 already-resurrected artifacts exist in origin/main HEAD. Do we need to manually re-delete them via prune-integrity or operator Git Data API push? Or does the next prune cycle handle it naturally? PROP-113's backfill_plan section should be expanded into a concrete procedure.

Other-side checks the operator already considered:
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Tinker already authored PROP-113; the design is there.' Counter: PROP-113's proposed_fix is philosophy + bash-fragment-level, not edit-level. The operator needs copy-pastable Edit-tool old_string/new_string blocks plus a smoke-test plan. Tinker has the audit + diff + clone discipline to produce those at higher fidelity than cowork-claude in a single session.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Just ship Fix A in cowork now — it's 5 lines.' Counter: ANY edit to workspace-sync.md is PROP-051 disaster-sensitive. The 2026-05-21 mass-delete was a 'small fallback path' that took out 14.9M lines. The discipline is: design, smoke-test plan, review, then ship. Skipping the design phase for a 'small' edit is exactly the pattern that produced the disaster.
- ARGUE-AGAINST: 'The resurrection loop isn't load-bearing — artifacts already in archive.' Counter: True for correctness but bloats monitor/integrity/ daily (~150 zombies/day = ~55K/year). More importantly, PROP-103's verification_pattern is currently FAILING (residue not 0) which means PROP-103 is wrongly marked implemented; the canary-driven auto-close mechanism (PROP-102) will eventually try to close PROPs based on verification_pattern grades — a wrongly-implemented PROP in the graph corrupts that mechanism's trust.
task: Author a comprehensive design document for PROP-113 fixes A/B/C suitable for operator review + selection. Include concrete bash diffs (Edit-tool old_string/new_string format), per-phase PROP-051-grade smoke-test procedures, disaster-vector analysis with detection + rollback for each, sequence recommendation with trade-off framing, and backfill cleanup plan for the 312 already-resurrected artifacts.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Map the exact insertion points. Read monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md and locate: (a) the existing GIT_DELETED_SET build block (the sort -u over archive JSONL extractions), (b) the existing GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED PROP-103 trust gate, (c) the existing fail-closed SKIP path that consumes GIT_DELETED_SET_UNTRUSTED, (d) the end-of-run report-writing step where Fix C would insert. Report line numbers and surrounding context for each.

Q2 — Fix A concrete diff. Produce the exact old_string/new_string for the two-sided trust gate. The new check should fire when `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > ARCHIVE_LINES` OR `GIT_DELETED_COUNT > 1.5*ARCHIVE_LINES` (recommend which threshold; PROP-113 mentions both — pick one and justify). Use the same UNTRUSTED sentinel write as PROP-103's existing gate. The diff should be self-contained — no other changes required for A alone to work.

Q3 — Fix B concrete diff. Produce the old_string/new_string for the robust set-build. This may require a helper Node script (similar to monitor/scripts/sync-workspace-step4c.js extraction pattern PROP-066 established) or can fit inline depending on length. If a helper is needed, write the script in full (no placeholders) and the bash one-liner that invokes it. Path-validation regex from PROP-113 (`^monitor/integrity/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$`) is the floor; tinker may widen/narrow with justification.

Q4 — Fix C concrete diff. Produce the old_string/new_string for the post-sync assertion. Locate the exact run-report-writing step in workspace-sync.md and insert the check-prune-resurrection.js invocation BEFORE the report's success-status is finalized. Define the sentinel file format for `workspace-sync-resurrection-abort-<ts>.json` (mirror existing `workspace-sync-abort-*.json` shape from PROP-051). Confirm `--hours 2` is the right narrow window or recommend an alternative (e.g., `--hours 1`).

Q5 — Disaster-vector analysis per fix. For each of A, B, C: (i) what's the worst-case failure mode if the fix has a bug? (ii) how would tinker (or operator) DETECT the bug on the next pipeline run? (iii) what's the rollback procedure (operator-side, since workspace-sync.md is git-owned)? Be specific — 'revert the commit' is not enough; what files need restoring, what scheduled task needs pausing, what sentinel proves rollback completed?

Q6 — Smoke-test procedure per phase. Define test cases that (a) exercise the bug pre-fix (current 70,375-overcount situation should still be reproducible in a sandbox if tinker can clone-and-replay), (b) verify the fix closes the bug, (c) verify no regression on the known-good cycle (a normal prune+sync produces RC=0 from check-prune-resurrection.js --hours 48). Tinker may write a dedicated test script `monitor/scripts/test-prop-113.js` if the smoke-test is complex enough.

Q7 — Sequence recommendation. Three phase candidates: (P1) ship A only and observe for 48h before deciding B+C; (P2) ship A+C (gate + assertion) without touching the set-build logic; (P3) ship A+B+C in one commit. PROP-113 implies P3 but the operator wants the trade-off framed: what's the leverage of each phase, what's the QA cost, what's the rollback complexity? Recommend one path with reasoning.

Q8 — Backfill cleanup. 312 artifacts already resurrected in origin/main. Options: (i) wait for next prune cycle to re-delete naturally; (ii) operator runs prune-integrity manually with a --force flag; (iii) operator pushes a one-shot delete via Git Data API (PROP-050 escape hatch). Recommend an option with the procedure. Note: the artifacts are in archive ledgers already, so the deletes don't lose data — they just need to leave the working tree.

Q9 — Integration with PROP-103 lifecycle. PROP-103 is currently marked 'implemented' but its verification_pattern step 5 is failing. Should PROP-113's landing automatically supersede PROP-103 (via supersedes_props on PROP-113)? Or should PROP-103 be left as a historical record + PROP-113 stand alone? PROP-102's auto-close mechanism needs to know which interpretation is right. Recommend with justification.
deliverable: An amendment to monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-113-gitdeletedset-overcount-trust-gap.json (status remains propose-only; this enriches the file with the design detail). The amendment should contain new sections: (1) Q1 insertion-point map; (2) Q2-Q4 concrete bash diffs for fixes A/B/C in Edit-tool format; (3) Q5 per-fix disaster-vector analysis with detection + rollback; (4) Q6 per-phase smoke-test procedure (with test-prop-113.js source if needed); (5) Q7 sequence recommendation with phase trade-offs; (6) Q8 backfill cleanup plan; (7) Q9 PROP-103 lifecycle resolution. Operator reads the amendment + ships the recommended phase.
constraints: Do NOT edit monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md as part of this analysis. The work is propose-only — author the diffs IN the PROP-113 file, don't apply them.
Honor PROP-051 disaster sensitivity throughout. Every fix must preserve the existing fail-closed behavior. New abort conditions must write sentinels that surface in the next integrity report.

If a helper Node script is needed (e.g., for Fix B set-build), write it in full in the PROP. Don't say 'a helper script would do X' — write the actual file contents the operator can drop into monitor/scripts/.

Don't extend scope. This directive is design-only for PROP-113 fixes A/B/C. If tinker discovers a related issue (e.g., another resurrection vector), file it as a separate PROP, don't fold it into the design.
Mirror PROP-110's question structure where the operator's options + trade-offs are surfaced explicitly. The operator's decision after reading this should be obvious-which-phase-to-pick.
